searchText: 100% agree. Stateless block production comes with too much complexity that aren't worth waiting for to have stateless nodes imo\. That's an interesting solution, though in practice the only nodes that are incentivized to be stateful will be block producers (they are forced to be) and perhaps indexers / archive nodes (though indexers don't need to be stateful per say). This seems like quite a quite small number of stateful nodes in a PoW world, does it not? This solution seems completely sufficient in a PoS world, but would be nice to have stateless node before the full PoS transition. <@!273808422753796097> did you see my proposal here for adjusting how transaction gossip works?: https://notes.ethereum.org/YtI7e-R5RSK13cklq8j3Ug?view hmm I'm not sure how this solves the stated problem (broadcasting reliably to miners) Can you explain more? There's an "assumption" that a client can attain a "proof" against the sending account. Based on that assumption, they can then construct the transaction, and broadcast it in the network described in my document along with the proof against a recent state root. That new gossip network then acts in much the same way as the current gossip network. Assuming either miners are part of the new gossip network, or there are nodes bridging between the new gossip network and the legacy one (`ETH` on DevP2P), then the transaction will eventually be gossiped to a miner. What do you mean by "a proof against the sending account" A witness that covers just the tx sender account? And that's sufficient to prove to the network that the tx can pay fees? validation of transaction means checking `nonce` and `balance`, so a merkle proof against tx.sender account right, that certainly is clever! (unless we're talking about account abstraction... which makes things complex) Where would these proofs come from? well, if the client is stateful, they can make it themselves. Infura could provide them. Or if we're successful in building the <#796057759858425866> network then they could easily be constructed from fetching data from there. right I see Or if the client happens to be directly connected to a stateful peer right, there could be a level of altruism where a peer might signal that they are willing to accept witness-less transactions and that they'll fill in the witness before forwarding. but in general, I like treating them as separate problems. From the perspective of the gossip network, it doesn't care where the proofs come from. And from the state network side, it doesn't care why people are looking up state data. got it yeah, the idea that you only need a witness for the tx sender is clever

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: hmm I'm not sure how this solves the stated problem (broadcasting reliably to miners)

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Can you explain more?

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: There's an "assumption" that a client can attain a "proof" against the sending account.  Based on that assumption, they can then construct the transaction, and broadcast it in the network described in my document along with the proof against a recent state root.  That new gossip network then acts in much the same way as the current gossip network.  Assuming either miners are part of the new gossip network, or there are nodes bridging between the new gossip network and the legacy one (`ETH` on DevP2P), then the transaction will eventually be gossiped to a miner.

excerpts.content: What do you mean by "a proof against the sending account"

excerpts.content: And that's sufficient to prove to the network that the tx can pay fees?

excerpts.content: validation of transaction means checking `nonce` and `balance`, so a merkle proof against tx.sender account
